lesson.title: The Line Is Tempting
lesson.hook: Two connected choices. Watch what your first shot creates.
lesson.liveIntro: You are pulled wide and behind the baseline on your backhand. The opposite sideline looks inviting.

tl1A.name: Choose from this contact, not the last one.
tl1A.sit: You used the extra flight time. Their reply now comes to your forehand.
tl1A.q: Choose from this contact, not the last one.

lines.A: You restore depth and cover the next angles. Still in play.
lines.B: You have room for controlled pressure here. Recover again after contact.

tl1A.take: An empty corner is only an opportunity if your contact supports the shot.
tl1A.payoff: An empty corner is only an opportunity if your contact supports the shot.
tl1A.principle: Balance before direction. Give yourself room to recover.
tl1A.why: A wide, low contact behind the baseline makes a direction change more demanding and leaves court to cover. Higher crosscourt play can buy recovery time. Judge the next shot from the new ball and balance, not from whether the previous attempt happened to land.

tl1B.name: Choose from this contact, not the last one.
tl1B.sit: Their crosscourt reply sends you a long way to the forehand. You are hurried.
tl1B.q: Choose from this contact, not the last one.

lines.A: The higher reply gives you another recovery window.
lines.B: It lands here, but pressing while hurried leaves little margin.

tl1.name: Does this contact support changing direction?
tl1.sit: You are pulled wide and behind the baseline on your backhand. The opposite sideline looks inviting.
tl1.q: Does this contact support changing direction?

lines.A: The higher crosscourt ball gives you time to cover. Read their next direction.
lines.B: You change direction while stretched. Their reply takes you across the court.

drill.name: Two-ball read
drill.how: Alternate a wide deep feed and a shorter central feed. Call “hold” or “change” before contact; recover and play the next ball.
